  "text": "For several breaths, no one moved. The water around Mara’s boots settled, and the last trickle through the gate stopped. Beyond it, something heavy scraped along the other side of the iron.

The harbor master lifted his pole. “Is it shut?”

The woman kept her bleeding hand against the lock. “For now.”

Out in the harbor, the man’s boat drifted back toward the quay. He made no effort to row. He was staring at the pale outline the photograph had left on the gate.

Mara leaned closer. Within the square, two darker marks had appeared, no larger than fingerprints. She looked at the woman, who wrapped her thumb in a strip torn from her sleeve.

“Who was in the picture?” Mara asked.

The woman glanced toward the boat. “Ask him.”

A knock came from the gate. The harbor master stumbled back, but the woman did not flinch. A second knock followed, softer and lower, near the broken hinge.

The man stepped from the boat onto the quay. Water poured from its seams, though the deck was dry. “There were three of us,” he said.

Mara looked again at the two marks. “Where’s the third?”

The bell began to swing without sounding. The woman caught Mara by the wrist and drew her away from the gate.

“On the wrong side,” the man said.

Behind the iron, a voice called Mara’s name. It sounded like her own voice, spoken through a mouthful of seawater."
